broker.name: OneRoyal
broker.tagline: On its own site since 2006. Its site names 4 regulators, including ASIC, CySEC, and FSA (St Vincent). Rules depend on where you live. Advertised leverage: Up to 1:1000.
broker.about: OneRoyal says it has operated since 2006. The pages checked do not name one headquarters. Account names on its site include ECN, Classic, Prime, Cent, Fixed Spread Classic, Fixed Spread ECN, and Fixed Spread Cent. Platforms named there include MetaTrader 4, MetaTrader 5, and Copy Trading. The site names these regulators: ASIC, CySEC, FSA (St Vincent), and VFSC. The company on an account depends on where the client lives. Minimum deposit is not a single number on the pages that loaded. The highest leverage figure taken from those pages is Up to 1:1000. Leverage increases losses as well as gains.

leverage.market: Variable spread accounts (ECN, Classic, Prime, Cent)
leverage.note: Homepage also advertises 1000x max leverage. The accounts navigation mentions dynamic leverage but the fetched text does not give a second maximum.

broker.leverage_note: Leverage increases losses as well as gains, and you can lose more than you deposit. The highest figure on this card is the highest number this broker advertises. It is not the cap on every account. The cap depends on the company, the product and where you live.

other_fees.label: Minimum deposit
other_fees.note: Variable-spread table on the accounts page: ECN $5, Classic $5, Prime $5,000, Cent $10. The same page says the minimum deposit may vary by payment provider and country of residence. No single minimum is stored.

other_fees.label: Financial Commission compensation fund
other_fees.note: Membership benefit stated on the licences page, not a trading fee. The fund is used if a member does not follow a Financial Commission judgment.
